To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a semiparametric approach to linkage analysis for diseases with age of onset.
we have developed a new semiparametric linkage method using pseudolikelihood ratio tests on neighbouring sets.
we propose a semiparametric method to incorporate age of onset information in linkage analysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new statistical methods for the linkage analysis of complex diseases with age of onset.
the use of multiple marker data and age of onset in a semiparametric model for linkage analysis.

the development of new statistical methods for linkage analysis of quantitative traits and disease phenotypes, and with applications of these methods to genetic data from the Framingham Heart Study and other sources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these new methods are more powerful than the existing methods for linkage analysis of age‐of‐onset data.
the proposed method is more powerful than the conventional methods, and the power of this method can be increased if we use more informative genetic markers.
the proposed methods provide an efficient way to utilize age of onset information for linkage analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed methods are able to detect linkage and age of onset effects simultaneously, and the proposed methods are more powerful than the existing approaches.
the new methods are more powerful than current methods for detecting linkage with genetic markers, and they can be applied to pedigrees with different numbers of affected and unaffected individuals.
, by incorporating age of onset information, the new linkage methods can be more powerful than current methods in linkage analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the age of onset is a useful tool to help detect linkage in complex disease.

the use of age of onset information can improve the power to detect linkage, especially in the case of late‐onset diseases, and the use of contrasts between affected and non‐affected individuals can improve the power for detecting linkage in the presence of heterogeneity.
age of onset information can be incorporated into linkage analysis using pseudolikelhoods on neighbouring sets.
